title: Longest run that can be made one letter with k changes
summary: With paint for only k tiles, find the longest stretch of a tiled wall that can be made a single colour.
goal: Find the longest stretch that can become one colour with at most k repaints

mapping.formal: Window size − count of its most common letter

examples.label: AABABBA, k = 1
examples.explanation: AABA becomes AAAA by repainting one B.

examples.label: ABAB, k = 2
examples.explanation: Repaint both A tiles (or both B tiles) to make the whole wall one colour.

examples.label: AAAA, k = 0
examples.explanation: The wall is already one colour.

ladder.name: Check every stretch
ladder.idea: For each start, extend the stretch tile by tile, keeping counts, and stop when it needs more than k repaints.

ladder.name: Slide a window with a tally
ladder.idea: Grow the window one tile at a time while tracking how many tiles share the most common colour. When it would need more than k repaints, slide it forward instead of growing.
ladder.insight: A stretch needs (size − most common count) repaints. We only want stretches longer than the best so far, so a window that breaks the rule can slide instead of shrinking.

approaches.name: Slide a window with a tally
approaches.summary: Grow; when repaints exceed k, slide the window one tile.

transfer.problem: A list of exam answers is either right or wrong. You may flip up to k wrong answers. What is the longest run of consecutive right answers you can make?
transfer.explanation: It is the same window: keep the stretch whose wrong answers number at most k, growing on the right and sliding when there are too many.

selfCheck: Computes repaints as window size minus the most common count.
Slides the window by one when it needs more than k repaints.
Returns the best size seen, not the final window size.
